In [[geometry]], the '''octagrammic prism''' is one of an infinite set of nonconvex [[Prism (geometry)|prisms]] formed by square sides and two regular [[star polygon]] caps, in this case two [[octagram]]s.
An octagrammic prism has 16 vertices, 2 [[octagram|octagrammic stars]], 8 square faces, and 24 edges.<ref>{{cite conference
 | last       = Huylebrouck
 | first      = Dirk
 | title      = Euler-Cayley Formula for ‘Unusual’ Polyhedra
 | book-title = Bridges 2016: Mathematics, Music, Art, Architecture, Education, Culture
 | pages      = 263–268
 | year       = 2016
 | url        = https://archive.bridgesmathart.org/2016/bridges2016-263.pdf
}}</ref>
